subject.title: Transcript redaction corrupts Anthropic/Bedrock reasoning signatures (AIza/LTAI false positive), causing persistent replay_invalid

question: Should OpenClaw treat validated Anthropic/Bedrock provider signature fields as opaque replay bytes even when their contents match credential-looking redaction patterns?
rationale: The narrow product bug is clear, but the fix changes the boundary between secret redaction and provider-owned opaque bytes; a maintainer needs to choose how much bypass is acceptable and how existing poisoned transcripts should be repaired.

options.title: Scoped structural preservation plus repair
options.body: Preserve only validated route-and-field-specific opaque replay tokens, keep credential redaction elsewhere, and drop/repair already corrupted thinking blocks before Bedrock/Anthropic replay.

options.title: Only tighten vendor regexes
options.body: Make case-sensitive and boundary-aware credential patterns to reduce false positives, but leave opaque signature preservation dependent on the generic redactor and risk other token-pattern false positives.

options.title: Rely on recovery only
options.body: Keep current redaction behavior and depend on replay_invalid recovery, accepting persistent poisoned transcript entries and continued intermittent turn loss.

recommendation.title: Scoped structural preservation plus repair
recommendation.body: Preserve only validated route-and-field-specific opaque replay tokens, keep credential redaction elsewhere, and drop/repair already corrupted thinking blocks before Bedrock/Anthropic replay.

likelyOwner.reason: Most directly tied to the merged opaque signature preservation boundary and the recent current-main maintenance of the implicated files.
